chunks: [The Virtue of Revelation/Prophethood:] I subdued the chiefs of the Arabs in my childhood, and broke the horn-points (i.e., defeated the leaders) of the tribes of Rabi'ah and Mudar.

And you know my position with the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) through close kinship and special status: He placed me in his lap while I was a child; he pressed me to his chest, enveloped me in his bed, touched my body with his, and let me smell his fragrance. He used to chew something and then feed it to me. He found no lie in my speech, nor weakness in my action.

key_terms.نَوَاجِمَ قُرُونِ: horn-points of the horns (metaphor for leaders/chiefs)

ai.seo_question: What does Nahj al-Balagha say about the childhood relationship between Ali and the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha underscores Ali ibn Abi Talib's unique spiritual and physical proximity to the Prophet Muhammad, highlighting the intimate upbringing (Tarbiyah) that prepared him for his role as the successor. It serves as a foundational Shia argument for Ali's innate truthfulness (Sidq) and reliability, rooted in the Prophet's direct, lifelong observation of his character from childhood. This close bond is often cited by scholars to illustrate the transmission of divine knowledge and authority through the Ahl al-Bayt.
